title: TORCH tests before pregnancy
what: This is a blood test from a vein. It shows if your body has met infections that are risky in pregnancy: toxoplasmosis, rubella, cytomegalovirus, and herpes.
why: When planning a pregnancy, usually 2 to 3 months before, and sometimes in early pregnancy.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come in a few days
tell_doctor: If you had a rubella vaccine
If you were recently ill or had a fever
If you have a cat at home

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Best in the morning before eating, or a few hours after a light meal. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: For 24 hours, no alcohol and no hard workouts. Best not to smoke in the morning.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide if anything should change.

bring: Your vaccination record, if you have it
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills a tube
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes and keep your arm straight
You can eat right away and go back to your usual day
Results usually come in a few days. The lab will tell you when
If you are not protected against rubella, your doctor may offer a vaccine before pregnancy

faq.q: What does a positive IgG mean?
faq.a: Usually it means you had the infection in the past and are protected. Your doctor will explain.

faq.q: When should I test if I am planning a pregnancy?
faq.a: Usually 2 to 3 months before, so there is time for a vaccine if needed.

reminders.text: TORCH test tomorrow. Best to come before eating. Water is fine.
